Do not breastfeed during and 1 week after

summary: Capmatinib is an oral MET kinase inhibitor for adults with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors have a mutation leading to mesenchymal-epithelial transition (MET) exon 14 skipping. The dose is 400 mg twice daily with or without food. Key risks are interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis (which can be fatal), hepatotoxicity, pancreatic enzyme elevation, and photosensitivity.
indications: Metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in adults whose tumors have a mutation leading to mesenchymal-epithelial transition (MET) exon 14 skipping, as detected by an FDA-approved test

dosage.c: Metastatic NSCLC with MET exon 14 skipping (adult)
dosage.n: Swallow tablets whole; with or without food; continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
Permanently discontinue if unable to tolerate 200 mg twice daily
Withhold if ILD suspected; discontinue if confirmed

admin: Swallow tablets whole; do not break, crush or chew
May be taken with or without food
Take at approximately the same times each day, about 12 hours apart
If a dose is vomited or missed, skip it and take the next dose at the scheduled time
moa: Capmatinib is an inhibitor of MET, including the mutant variant produced by exon 14 skipping. MET exon 14 skipping leads to a protein with decreased turnover and resultant increased MET signaling. Capmatinib inhibits MET phosphorylation triggered by ligand binding or MET amplification, as well as MET-mediated downstream signaling and proliferation of tumor cells dependent on MET.

relative: Significant hepatic impairment (not studied in severe)
monitor: Concomitant strong CYP3A inhibitors or inducers
Drugs sensitive to P-gp or BCRP transport

preg: Based on its mechanism and animal findings, capmatinib can cause fetal harm. Advise pregnant women of the potential risk to a fetus. Females of reproductive potential should use effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the final dose; verify pregnancy status before starting.
lact: There are no data on the presence of capmatinib in human milk or its effects on the breastfed child or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the final dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild to moderate renal impairment. The pharmacokinetics in severe renal impairment or end-stage renal disease have not been studied.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild or moderate hepatic impairment. Capmatinib has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment. Monitor liver function tests; hepatotoxicity can be serious. Withhold, reduce, or discontinue based on the severity of transaminase/bilirubin elevations.

major: Strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole) - increase capmatinib exposure and toxicity; monitor and reduce dose if needed
Strong and moderate CYP3A inducers (e.g., rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St. John's wort) - decrease capmatinib exposure; avoid coadministration
moderate: P-gp substrates (e.g., digoxin) - capmatinib may increase their concentrations; monitor for toxicity
BCRP substrates (e.g., rosuvastatin, sulfasalazine) - capmatinib may increase their concentrations; monitor
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; a high-fat meal does not have a clinically meaningful effect on exposure.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol owing to additive potential for hepatotoxicity.
interactions.diagnostics: May increase ALT, AST, bilirubin, amylase and lipase; may cause lymphopenia and decreased albumin.

serious: Interstitial lung disease / pneumonitis (can be fatal)
Increased amylase and lipase / pancreatitis risk
emergency: Acute interstitial lung disease / pneumonitis with respiratory failure

monitoring: Pulmonary symptoms (dyspnea, cough, fever) - evaluate promptly for ILD/pneumonitis
Liver function tests (ALT, AST, total bilirubin) before starting, every 2 weeks during the first 3 months, then monthly or as indicated
Disease response and tolerance for dose modification
counsel: Take twice daily about 12 hours apart, with or without food; swallow whole
Report any new or worsening shortness of breath, cough, or fever right away (lung inflammation)
Report yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine or right-sided abdominal pain (liver injury)
Avoid prolonged sun exposure; use sunscreen and protective clothing (photosensitivity)
Use effective non-hormonal contraception; do not breastfeed during and for 1 week after the last dose
pk: Inhibits MET signaling rapidly after absorption
Twice-daily dosing maintains exposure; steady state by day 3
pearls: Indicated only for MET exon 14 skipping NSCLC confirmed by an FDA-approved test
ILD/pneumonitis can be fatal - any new respiratory symptom warrants prompt evaluation and treatment interruption
Avoid strong/moderate CYP3A inducers; they substantially lower capmatinib levels
Counsel on photosensitivity and sun protection
missed: If a dose is missed or the patient vomits after taking a dose, do not make up the dose; take the next dose at the regularly scheduled time.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for capmatinib overdose. Management consists of stopping the drug and providing general supportive care with monitoring of organ function (especially pulmonary and hepatic) and treatment of symptoms.
